title: Lucy (13 December)
hook: a Sicilian martyr whose name sounds like light, honored with candles in dark Scandinavia

segments.voice: Yesterday, Santa Casa and the small stone room. Your line was the holy house.

It's still pitch dark outside on a December morning in Sweden. A door opens and a girl in a long white dress walks in, slowly, because she's wearing a crown of lit candles on her head. Behind her comes a line of others in white, each holding one candle, singing. Families, schools and churches in Sweden and its neighbors keep some version of this morning. The girl is dressed as a saint. Not a Viking, not a winter spirit. A young martyr from Sicily, a long way south. Her name is Lucy.
screen: `A DARK SWEDISH MORNING.` → `A CROWN OF CANDLES.` → `A SAINT FROM SICILY.`

segments.voice: Lucy was a martyr of Syracuse, in Sicily. Like Cecilia last week, she is one of the women martyrs named in the Roman Canon, the first Eucharistic Prayer of the Roman Missal. Beyond her name, her story comes from her legend. She decides to give her life to God, and she gives her dowry away to the poor. The young man she was expected to marry is furious and reports her as a Christian. The authorities try to drag her off to shame her, and in the legend they cannot move her at all. Not with ropes, not with a team of oxen. She stands there like a pillar. She dies by the sword. Now, the light. Lucy's name sounds like lux, the Latin for light, and the people who told her story leaned into it. Paintings show her holding a lamp, or carrying her eyes on a dish, and she became the patron of people with trouble seeing. Her feast falls in the dark weeks of the northern winter, and some say that is part of why the north took her to heart. John's gospel puts it in one line. In the Douay-Rheims: "And the light shineth in darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it." The Lucy morning acts that verse out. Somebody walks into the dark room carrying light, and the room doesn't get to stay dark. A martyr who gave her dowry away became, far from home, the girl who brings the morning in.
screen: `A MARTYR OF SYRACUSE.` · `HER DOWRY GIVEN TO THE POOR.` · `THEY CANNOT MOVE HER.` · `A NAME THAT SOUNDS LIKE LIGHT.` · then, large: `AND THE LIGHT SHINETH IN DARKNESS.`

segments.voice: If you have a candle and it's safe, light it now; if not, sit in a dim spot and switch on one small lamp, and notice how far one small light reaches, and where it stops. If you pray, hold the people in your life who are in a dark stretch right now, one at a time, in that light; if you don't, simply stay with the glow.
Lucy. The martyr of Syracuse who gave her dowry to the poor, whose feast brings candles into the dark weeks of December.
Your line: light in december. One small flame, and the darkest morning changes. Rest well.

howItsDone: Saint Lucy is remembered on 13 December; in Sweden and other Nordic countries the day is kept with processions of singers in white led by a girl wearing a crown of candles, and in Sicily with special foods and Masses.
